subject: Civil Engineering
title: Beam Bridges: The Simplest Span
description: A fast breakdown of Beam Bridges: The Simplest Span for builders.

hook.text: A plank laid across a ditch is the oldest bridge design. It still works.

buildup.text: Beam bridges rest on supports at each end. The beam bends under its own load.

discovery.text: Steel I-beams or concrete box girders make modern beam bridges span up to 250 feet.

twist.text: Beyond that, the beam's weight becomes the problem — it starts crushing itself.

climax.text: Highway overpasses are almost always beam bridges — simple, fast, and reliable.

punchline.text: The beam bridge is boring — and that's why it works.

quiz.question: What limits the span of a simple beam bridge?
options: The beam's own weight causes excessive bending at longer spans
Government regulations restrict beam bridge lengths
